answer: A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The dune multiplier is published, charged in lagoon, and wander lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 11 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 1392 identities would post 1556 proofs and burn roughly 64 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
